articles.summary: 3D Systems Announces Agreements to Exchange All Outstanding 5.875% Convertible Senior Secured Notes Due 2030, Eliminating All Secured Debt Rachael Dalton… Wed, 11/04/2026 - 21:08 Release Date Wednesday, Nov 4, 2026 9:08 PM ROCK HILL, South Carolina, November 4, 2026 – 3D Systems Corporation (NYSE: DDD) (“3D Systems” or the “Company”) today announced that it has entered into separate, privately negotiated exchange agreements with all of the holders (the “Transaction Participants”) of its currently outstanding 5.875% convertible senior secured notes due 2030 (the “2030 Notes”). Pursuant to these exchange agreements, the Company has agreed to exchange $92,030,000 aggregate principal amount of 2030 Notes held by the Transaction Participants, representing all of the outstanding 2030 Notes, for $85,000,000 aggregate principal amount of newly issued 3.30% convertible senior notes due 2031 (the “2031 Notes”), 13,471,138 shares (the “Shares”) of the Company’s common stock and $20,000,000 in cash, plus accrued and unpaid interest on the exchanged 2030 Notes to, but excluding, the closing date, subject to certain adjustments if the closing occurs after December 1, 2026 (the “Exchange”). The 2031 Notes will be senior unsecured obligations of the Company, will bear interest at a rate of 3.30% per year, payable semiannually in arrears on April 1 and October 1 of each year, beginning on April 1, 2027, and will mature on April 1, 2031, unless earlier converted, redeemed or repurchased. The 2031 Notes will be convertible into cash, shares of the Company’s common stock or a combination of cash and shares, at the Company’s election, at an initial conversion rate of 291.3753 shares of common stock per $1,000 principal amount of 2031 Notes (equivalent to an initial conversion rate of approximately $3.43 per share of common stock, which represents a premium of approximately 30.0% over the last reported sale price of the Company’s common stock on the New York Stock Exchange on November 4, 2026 of $2.64 per share), subject to certain adjustments. The Exchange is expected to close on or about November 12, 2026, subject to certain closing conditions. Assuming all of the 2030 Notes are exchanged, upon the closing of the Exchange, no 2030 Notes will be outstanding, and the Company expects that the indenture governing the 2030 Notes will be satisfied and discharged and the related guarantees and the liens on the collateral securing the 2030 Notes will be released. 3D Systems will not receive any cash proceeds from the Exchange. This announcement is neither an offer to sell nor a solicitation of an offer to buy any of the Shares, the 2031 Notes or any shares of common stock issuable upon conversion of the 2031 Notes, nor shall there be any offer, solicitation or sale in any jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful prior to registration or qualification under applicable securities laws. The offer and sale of the Shares, the 2031 Notes and any shares of common stock issuable upon conversion of the 2031 Notes have not been, and will not be, registered under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, or qualified under any state securities laws and may not be offered or sold in the United States absent registration or an applicable exemption from such registration or qualification requirements. articles.summary: 3D Systems Announces a Year of Milestones in 3D Printing Culminating at Formnext 2026 Kara Caldwell Mon, 11/16/2026 - 16:26 Release Date Monday, Nov 16, 2026 4:30 PM New MultiJet, wax material and direct metal 3D printing technologies and software releases at Formnext 2026 round out the company’s efforts for 2026 Focused investments and strategies in aerospace & defense, healthcare and dental markets deliver advanced tools and technologies to customers Visit 3D Systems at Formnext 2026, November 17-20, booth D11 in Hall 11.0 ROCK HILL, South Carolina, Nov 16, 2026 – 3D Systems (NYSE:DDD) today announced the release of the MJP 300 multijet 3D printer, the new TSR (Transport-Sieve-Reload) powder management systems for direct metal 3D printing, and upgrades to the 3D Sprint software including digital rights management (DRM) tools. In addition, 3D Systems continues to build on key investments in 3D printed Jetted Denture systems, healthcare solutions, as well as strategic partnerships and expanded facilities for Aerospace & Defense manufacturing. “We have spent the last eighteen months on targeted, focused investments in people, facilities, materials and technologies that reflect where the true growth and demand is for 3D printing – namely healthcare, dental, and aerospace & defense,” said Dr. Jeff Graves, president and CEO, 3D Systems. “As a result we have achieved numerous strategic milestones including the release of and clearance for the NextDent Jetted Denture solution, the release of the MJP 300W Plus wax casting pattern system, numerous FDA and EU clearances for 3D printed healthcare solutions, new Stereolithography platforms, and an expansion of our production facilities for aerospace & defense customers. These latest announcements at Formnext are a result of that targeted strategy and effort to deliver ground-breaking solutions to our customers.” At Formnext 2026, 3D Systems is rounding out the year’s product developments with the following new offerings:. The new MJP 300 plastic 3D Printer delivers next-generation productivity The MJP 300 is a next-generation machine targeted at faster and easier operation for rapid production of plastic 3D printed parts. Additional build modes on this model allow for choices between sharper and smoother parts or increased speed of production. The MJP 300 incorporates enhanced cybersecurity features designed to support compliance with ESA/IEC standards, upgraded electronics for faster data processing, as well as new software and fleet management tools. This 3D printer builds on the renowned reliability of 3D Systems MJP technology as well as delivering new levels of efficiency in reduced use of support materials and easier, hands-free post-processing steps. Key features of the MJP 300 include: M2P-CST Crystal material now in both XHD, and with a very high-speed HD mode for high-definition parts Growing M2R materials suite to add XHD for a finer resolution mode for each material. HD, UHD (Ultra HD) and XHD (extreme High resolution) build modes deliver parts with 16 micron layers at 1600 x 900 dpi. With the ability to build large parts across the volume of the MJP 300 (294 x 211 x 144 mm, or 11.6 x 8.3 x 5.6 in) the system has the unique ability to divide the volume into 3 lanes. This enables small or tall parts to be grouped in a single lane for maximum production speed without sacrificing quality. 5 VisiJet® acrylate materials initially supported including M2P-Crystal, M2R-WH, M2R-CL, M2R-TN, M2R-HT90 with more to follow. Supported by the industry-leading 3D Sprint printer management software which now includes .finite, a Digital Rights Management (DRM) tool for protecting the Intellectual Property of your 3D data. Operates within the new AddiTrak™ fleet management software from 3D Systems for the monitoring and management of your 3D Systems machines. “The MJP 300 represents a new generation in multijet 3D printing,” said Martin Johnson, Vice President, Product & Technical Fellow, 3D Systems. ”Updated electronics and software provide a new level of accuracy, surface finish, ease-of-use and security for our customers with a platform that can scale.” The MJP 300 will be on display at Formnext 2026 and available to purchase in the first quarter of 2027. TSR: Closed-Loop Metal Powder Management, From Recovery to Reuse The TSR (Transport-Sieve-Reload) module is a mobile, closed-loop powder management solution, that can be connected to DMP Flex 350 metal 3D printers to enable powder recovery, sieving, and recirculation under inert conditions. This integrated workflow preserves powder quality for reuse while minimizing operator contact with the powder and maintaining inert conditions throughout the process. The solution combines 3D Systems innovations with proven powder handling technology from Russell Finex. A single TSR module can be shared across multiple compatible printers and is the latest addition to 3D Systems' powder management workflow options for the DMP Flex 350 platform. "Every metal additive manufacturing operation is different. That's why we've developed a flexible powder management portfolio that allows customers to choose the approach that best fits their production environment, operational requirements, and growth plans,” said Martin Johnson. “By combining 3D Systems’ innovations with proven technologies from trusted industry partners, such as Russell Finex, we're helping customers build on existing operations and implement workflows that adapt as their needs evolve. At Formnext, we are showcasing our TSR solution, which enables metal 3D powder recovery, sieving, and recirculation within a fully integrated inert workflow, maintaining low-oxygen conditions throughout the recovery and reuse cycle." The TSR module is available for purchase. 3D Sprint software update delivers new cybersecurity and DRM features 3D Systems’ professional-grade 3D print software has been updated to enable new cybersecurity and digital rights management tools for 3D Systems’ latest 3D printer releases. The .finite™ toolset available within 3D Sprint Pro protects the intellectual property of your 3D print data by helping prevent unauthorized access to your data as it is shared, limiting tampering and verifying data integrity, and securing the amount of 3D prints that can be made by specific workstations within controlled timelines. .finite will be initially available for the MJP 300W wax 3D printer , and the MJP 300 acrylate 3D printer, with more models to be supported in early 2027. New Industrial Wax Kit for MJP 300W Plus for 3D printed wax casting patterns Since its release in Q3 2025, the MJP 300W Plus has been an industry leader in the production of wax casting patterns for jewelry due to its ease-of-use, efficiency, precision and high reliability. As a result of high interest in the use of this system to produce larger wax casting patterns for industries such as aerospace, 3D Systems has released a new Industrial Wax kit which enables use of the VisiJet Wax Jewel Red material for this purpose. “This machine has already gained significant adoption for its ability to produce very detailed, fine geometry in wax for jewelry but has also turned the heads of the aerospace community for its ability to easily and quickly produce larger wax casting patterns with high accuracy and great surface finish,” said Johnson. ‘Using the VisiJet® Wax Jewel Red for larger parts is a natural evolution for this material which is highly ductile, durable and flexible.” This new Industrial Wax kit is available now. You can see all these new products, and more, at 3D Systems’ booth D11 in Hall 11.0 . Since then, that same spark continues to ignite the 3D Systems team as we work side-by-side with our customers to change the way industries innovate. As a full-service solutions partner, we deliver industry-leading 3D printing technologies, materials, and software to high-value markets such as medical and dental; aerospace, space and defense; transportation and motorsports; data center infrastructure; and durable goods. Each application-specific solution is powered by the expertise and passion of our employees who endeavor to achieve our shared goal of Transforming Manufacturing for a Better Future. articles.summary: 3D Systems Celebrates 40 Years During Formnext 2026 Kara Caldwell Thu, 11/12/2026 - 16:32 Release Date Thursday, Nov 12, 2026 4:30 PM The inventor of 3D printing to highlight the history and the future of 3D printing at key industry trade show Recognition for the early innovators across the industry who helped build the additive industry Visit booth D11 in Hall 11 at Formnext to see new developments in MultiJet 3D printing, Direct Metal 3D printing and more. ROCK HILL, South Carolina, November 12, 2026 – 3D Systems (NYSE:DDD) today announced plans to celebrate, at Formnext 2026, the 40th anniversary of the founding of 3D Systems and 43 years of the invention of SLA 3D printing by co-founder Chuck Hull. With guest appearances by Chuck Hull and opportunities to see and touch the original 3D-printed part, attendees can understand the origins of additive manufacturing, combined with 3D Systems’ vision of the future of manufacturing. “The 3D printing industry has grown steadily to more than $16B at the end of 2025 after more than 40 years of existence in large part thanks to Chuck Hull and 3D Systems,” said Scott Dunham, Executive Vice President of Research at Additive Manufacturing Research . “Chuck's dedication to this industry, and in turn 3D Systems' ongoing development of many foundational technologies, is commendable. Our projections for additive manufacturing estimate an industry of at least $65B by 2035, which is incredible when put into the context of beginning from one man's idea for a rapid prototyping technology.” While Chuck Hull has always been very humble about his own invention of SLA, he has also been admiring of innovations that came after, either via 3D Systems or from other inventors who have been either partners or competitors to 3D Systems, all of whom helped build the industry to where it is now. “This is a true celebration for 3D Systems, but also the 3D printing industry as a whole,” said Chuck Hull, inventor of 3D printing, CTO and co-founder of 3D Systems. “Turning this small idea into a $16 billion industry has been the result of hard work and a drive to succeed by many in the industry. The drive of entrepreneurship and innovation by everyone is what has made this industry grow and we want to celebrate that.” The Emergence of Competition in 3D Printing Following the commercialization of SLA, other key inventors emerged with different approaches to solving additive manufacturing. Scott Crump invented and patented Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) 3D printing in 1988, and with his wife, Lisa Crump, co-founded Stratasys (NASDAQ: SSYS). Stratasys provided an alternative to SLA 3D printing and rapid prototyping, helping to develop and expand the industry alongside 3D Systems. “We are excited to join Chuck Hull in this celebration of the 3D printing industry,” said Scott Crump, co-founder and Board Member of Stratasys. “Watching it grow from a series of bright ideas into a vital additive manufacturing industry has been incredibly fulfilling. None of it would have been possible without the passion and drive of pioneers like Chuck Hull and the many others who have helped make the industry what it is today.” In the 1980s, Carl R. Deckard, an undergraduate student at The University of Texas at Austin, conceived the idea for Selective Laser Sintering (SLS), a process that uses a laser to fuse powdered material into solid objects. He continued developing the idea through his master’s and doctoral studies under Dr. Joseph Beaman, his professor and mentor. Beaman recognized Carl’s talent and gave him the support, technical guidance, and freedom to explore that helped turn his idea into a working manufacturing process. DTM was acquired by 3D Systems in 2001. “Carl came up with a wild idea of making parts as he watched Star Trek one night and thought about the special effects of using sand as a backdrop when ‘beaming down’ to the planet. We worked on the idea and brought it to Joe who helped him make it work. It took quite a bit of dedication from both of them to get SLS out of the lab and into the market,” said David K. Leigh, a fellow student and colleague of Deckard’s. “DTM Corporation licensed the technology from UT Austin and developed it for commercial use. Carl died in 2019 at just 58. We lost him too soon, but the work he and Joe did together continues to make a difference today.” Another influential figure from the industry’s origins is Joe Allison, who joined 3D Systems in 1987 and filed 12 patents for the company across 3 years. He later formed Solid Concepts, which quickly became one of the world’s largest suppliers of 3D printed parts. Allison is now CEO of Gentle Giant Studios, a leading 3D printing and digital art company involved in the movie business. “Chuck Hull not only invented a technology but he founded an industry that has profoundly changed the way things are manufactured,” said Allison. “3D printing has repeatedly proven itself as the way forward for highly complex parts where the limitations of traditional manufacturing have been a barrier. We will see the industry continue to grow and develop in ways that no one can predict.” There are yet more inventors who have been and continue to be key influencers in the industry and so acknowledgement also goes to individuals including: Max Lebovsky, CEO, Formlabs; Andy Christensen, founder of Medical Modeling; Yoav Zeif, CEO, Stratasys; Emanuel Sachs who first invented binder jetting 3D printing; and many many more. From the History to the Future of 3D Printing Across the last 4 decades, the 3D printing industry has seen periods of growth and decline, optimism and doubt, but through the belief and innovation of many in the industry, it has grown far beyond what many would have expected. Chuck Hull continues to inspire new innovations in the industry. “3D printing continues to strengthen because of the inventiveness of people in applying it, perfecting the materials and processes,” said Dr. Jeff Graves, President & CEO, 3D Systems. “We have entered an era where 3D printing is now enabling unheard-of performance in space, automotive, dental and medical fields. With 3D printing, the sky is not the limit.” Attendees at Formnext will be able to hear Chuck Hull present alongside Patrick Dunne, SVP, Advanced Applications, 3D Systems, at 3.45 pm on Tuesday November 17, 2026 on the Technology Stage, Stand #B49 in Hall 12.1. You can join 3D Systems in celebrating both the last 40 years and the future of 3D printing at Formnext between 5 – 8 pm, Booth D11 in Hall 11, November 18 2026, Frankfurt, Germany About 3D Systems For 40 years Chuck Hull’s curiosity and desire to improve the way products were designed and manufactured gave birth to 3D printing, 3D Systems, and the additive manufacturing industry. Since then, that same spark continues to ignite the 3D Systems team as we work side-by-side with our customers to change the way industries innovate. As a full-service solutions partner, we deliver industry-leading 3D printing technologies, materials and software to high-value markets such as medical and dental; aerospace, space and defense; transportation and motorsports; data center infrastructure; and durable goods. Each application-specific solution is powered by the expertise and passion of our employees who endeavor to achieve our shared goal of Transforming Manufacturing for a Better Future. articles.summary: Breakthrough Technologies with 3D Systems at Formnext 2026 Anna Daugherty Wed, 11/25/2026 - 10:26 3D Systems at Formnext 2026 Always an incredible opportunity to showcase the latest innovations from 3D Systems, Formnext 2026 was a success for our team as we highlighted breakthrough technologies, explored real-world production applications , and connected with other industry experts and enthusiasts. Take a look at what we presented during the tradeshow and learn more about how 3D Systems is helping companies unlock new levels of performance with additive manufacturing. New Technology and MJP Advancements During the event, 3D Systems announced the release of our new MJP 300 multijet 3D printer , our new TSR (Transport-Sieve-Reload) powder management systems for direct metal 3D printing , and upgrades to the 3D Sprint software including digital rights management (DRM) tools. Additionally, 3D Systems has released a new Industrial Wax Kit, enabling use of the VisiJet Wax Jewel Red material for industries such as aerospace due to being highly ductile, durable and flexible. With focused investments and strategies in aerospace & defense , healthcare and dental markets, 3D Systems is committed to delivering advanced tools and technologies to customers. Attendees at formnext were invited to our booth to see these new innovations up-close and ask our team additional questions about their capabilities. 40 Years of 3D Printing Marking the 40th anniversary of the founding of 3D Systems and 43 years of the invention of SLA 3D printing by co-founder Chuck Hull, an exclusive 40th Anniversary celebration for team members, partners, and customers was held in our formnext booth. A 3D-printed life-size SLA model of Chuck Hull was on display for the show and formnext attendees were able to hold the first 3D-printed part to immerse themselves in the origins of additive manufacturing. Next-Generation Innovations: ETH Zurich Hyperloop Model With a commitment to the future of additive manufacturing, attendees were invited to discover how pellet-based additive manufacturing is supporting the development of next-generation hyperloop technologies and unlocking new opportunities for large-format manufacturing applications. A hyperloop prototype model was hosted in our booth to help attendees visualize how ETH Zürich utilized our EXT Titan Pellet 3D printing technology for production of their hyperloop prototype, leading to six awards at the European Hyperloop Week 2026. Informative Sessions of the Industry's Latest Formnext attendees were able to take advantage of educational sessions on leading additive manufacturing initiatives! 3D Systems held 3 speaking sessions that were highly attended and engaging for audience members, 'The First Layer: From Rapid Prototyping to Additive Manufacturing and Beyond' with Chuck Hull, Co-founder & CTO, 3D Systems & Patrick Dunne, SVP & Technical Fellow, 3D Systems 'Direct Multi-Jet 3D Printing of Internally-Cooled Turbine Blade Patterns for Investment Casting' with Patrick Dunne, SVP & Technical Fellow, 3D Systems 'Advancing Hyperloop Innovation with Pellet-Based Additive Manufacturing' with André Metzger, Channel Sales Manager, 3D Systems & James Schatzmann, Mechanical Engineering Student, Swissloop/ETH Zürich After the sessions, attendees were invited to meet us at our booth to discuss these innovations further with our team members! Dental and Healthcare Innovations from 3D Systems With technologies from 3D Systems enabling major advancements in the dental and medtech industries, customers and partners were invited to discover more about our innovative selection of 3D-printing solutions to fit your needs, including the dental industry’s first multi-material, multi-shade monolithic jetted denture solution. Looking Ahead to 2027 From concept to production, we appreciated the opportunity to introduce our latest innovations and how they are driving the future of manufacturing. We appreciate all of the formnext attendees that made this year's show a success for 3D Systems! Our team members find valuable connections each year with customers and partners at this exciting event and we look forward to continuing these conversations into 2027. articles.summary: 3D Systems Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results Kara Caldwell Wed, 11/04/2026 - 16:07 Release Date Wednesday, Nov 4, 2026 4:10 PM ROCK HILL, South Carolina - November 4, 2026 - 3D Systems Corporation (NYSE:DDD) announced today its financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. Q3 2026 revenue of $99.3 million, up 9% year-over-year, and up 11% excluding software divestitures, driven by double-digit growth in new printer and parts manufacturing sales and strong dental materials revenue. Net loss was $33.5 million for the quarter, while Adjusted EBITDA improved to $3.1 million, reflecting the benefits of prior cost reduction initiatives, higher sales volumes, and improved operating leverage in the quarter. Healthcare revenue increased 14% year-over-year, driven by continued growth in personalized healthcare solutions, and more than 20% growth in both healthcare parts manufacturing and dental materials sales. Industrial revenue increased 4% year-over year, or 8% excluding software divestitures, driven by strong growth in Data Center Infrastructure and more than 50% growth in Aerospace & Defense, partially offset by declines in consumer-facing markets. Our four strategic markets delivered strong double-digit growth through the first three quarters of 2026, advancing our strategy to accelerate growth in Med Tech, Dental, Aerospace & Defense and Data Center Infrastructure. Summary Comments on Results Dr. Jeffrey Graves, President and Chief Executive Officer of 3D Systems, said, “We are pleased with our third-quarter and year-to-date performance. Revenue growth accelerated, Adjusted EBITDA turned positive for the quarter and the year-to-date period, and our four strategic markets, Med Tech, Dental, Aerospace & Defense, and Data Center Infrastructure, continued to deliver strong double-digit growth. These results reflect the progress we have made executing a focused strategy: concentrating resources on high-value production applications, refreshing our product portfolio, and expanding our metal parts manufacturing capability. Customers in these markets are increasingly adopting 3D printing as a core manufacturing technology, and the combination of design flexibility and production economics is enabling higher-performance components and systems to move into full production.” Dr. Graves concluded, “As the additive manufacturing industry begins to emerge from a multi-year downturn, the consistent investments we have made in technology, application expertise, and production capacity during this challenging period have positioned the Company to benefit from the recovery. While the broader economic and geopolitical environment remains volatile, capital investment in our priority markets is now strengthening, and we are well positioned to support the resulting increase in demand for manufacturing capacity. I am confident in the foundation we have built and in the Company’s ability to deliver profitable growth in the years ahead.” "Our positive third-quarter results demonstrate continued progress against the priorities we established over the past two years,” said Phyllis Nordstrom, Chief Financial Officer of 3D Systems. “We delivered strong revenue growth while maintaining effective cost management, resulting in positive Adjusted EBITDA year-to-date. At the same time, we are steadily reshaping our business around our four strategic markets through the first three quarters of the year. Our year-to-date performance gives us confidence that our strategy is gaining traction and creating a stronger foundation for profitable growth." Third Quarter 2026 Results Total revenue increased 8.8% to $99.3 million compared to the prior year period. Excluding the impact of software divestitures completed in 2025, including 3DXpert and Oqton, total revenue increased by 10.9%. Healthcare Solutions revenue increased approximately 14.4% to $49.0 million compared to the prior year period. Revenue growth was primarily driven by higher dental material sales and increased parts manufacturing volumes. Industrial Solutions revenue increased approximately 3.9% to $50.3 million compared to the prior year period, or increased7.7% excluding the impact of software divestitures, primarily driven by higher printer and parts manufacturing sales. Gross profit margin increased to 35.0% compared to 32.3% in the prior year period. Non-GAAP gross profit margin increased to 35.5% compared to 32.5% in the prior year period. Adjusting for software divestitures, non-GAAP gross profit margin increased by 420 basis points. Non-GAAP gross profit margin benefited from higher sales volumes in printers and parts manufacturing, product gross profit margin expansion, and the non-recurrence of certain prior-year costs associated with a non-core site closure and a Reg Med accounting adjustment. Net loss attributable to 3D Systems Corporation increased by $15.5 million to $33.5 million, compared to the prior year period. The increase was primarily the result of litigation expense, an asset impairment charge, an unfavorable foreign exchange impact, and an unfavorable year-over-year change in income taxes. Adjusted EBITDA improved by $13.9 million, to $3.1 million compared to the prior year period, driven primarily by the impact of prior cost reduction initiatives, higher sales volumes in the quarter, and improved operating leverage in the quarter. Excluding the impact of software divestitures, Adjusted EBITDA improved $13.1 million. Financial Liquidity At September 30, 2026, the Company had total cash and investments of $120.5 million, which included cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash of $91.8 million, short-term investments of $27.1 million, and long-term investments of $1.6 million. A total of $3.9 million in principal amount of debt is scheduled to mature in the fourth quarter of 2026, with the remaining $92.0 million principal maturing in 2030. Fourth Quarter 2026 Outlook Revenue: $100 - $103 million Adjusted EBITDA: ($2) million - $0 million The fourth-quarter outlook reflects continued positive momentum across the Company’s four strategic markets, while incorporating normal variability in customer program and investment cycles and more evenly distributed purchasing patterns we observed throughout the year. At the midpoint of our fourth-quarter outlook, the Company expects full year revenue growth approaching mid-single digits for 2026. 3D Systems does not provide forward-looking guidance for certain measures on a GAAP basis. The Company is unable to provide a quantitative reconciliation of forward-looking Adjusted EBITDA to the most directly comparable forward-looking GAAP measures without unreasonable effort because certain items, including litigation expenses, acquisition expenses, stock-based compensation expense, intangible amortization expense, restructuring expenses, and goodwill impairment, are difficult to predict and estimate. These items are inherently uncertain and depend on various factors, many of which are beyond the Company’s control, and as such, any associated estimate and its impact on GAAP performance could vary materially. About 3D Systems For 40 years, Chuck Hull’s curiosity and desire to improve the way products were designed and manufactured gave birth to 3D printing, 3D Systems, and the additive manufacturing industry. Since then, that same spark continues to ignite the 3D Systems team as we work side-by-side with our customers to change the way industries innovate. As a full-service solutions partner, we deliver industry-leading 3D printing technologies, materials and software to high-value markets such as medical and dental; aerospace, space and defense; transportation and motorsports; data center infrastructure; and durable goods. Each application-specific solution is powered by the expertise and passion of our employees who endeavor to achieve our shared goal of Transforming Manufacturing for a Better Future. More information on the Company is available at www.3dsystems.com. 3D SYSTEMS CORPORATION Reconciliations of GAAP to Non-GAAP Measures Presentation of Information in this Press Release 3D Systems reports its financial results in accordance with GAAP. Management also reviews and reports certain non-GAAP measures, including: adjusted revenue, non-GAAP gross profit, non-GAAP gross profit margin, non-GAAP diluted income (loss) per share, non-GAAP operating expense and Adjusted EBITDA. These non-GAAP measures exclude certain items that management does not view as part of 3D Systems’ core results as they may be highly variable, may be unusual or infrequent, are difficult to predict and can distort underlying business trends and results. Management believes that the non-GAAP measures provide useful additional insight into underlying business trends and results and provide meaningful information regarding the comparison of period-over-period results. Additionally, management uses the non-GAAP measures for planning, forecasting and evaluating business and financial performance, including allocating resources and evaluating results relative to employee compensation targets. 3D Systems’ non-GAAP measures are not calculated in accordance with or as required by GAAP and may not be calculated in the same manner as similarly titled measures used by other companies. These non-GAAP measures should thus be considered as supplemental in nature and not considered in isolation or as a substitute for the related financial information prepared in accordance with GAAP. To calculate the non-GAAP measures, 3D Systems excludes the impact of the following items: amortization of intangible assets, a non-cash expense, as 3D Systems’ intangible assets were primarily acquired in connection with business combinations; costs incurred in connection with acquisitions and divestitures, such as legal, consulting and advisory fees; stock-based compensation expenses, a non-cash expense; charges related to restructuring and cost optimization plans, impairment charges, including goodwill, and divestiture gains or losses; the impact of software divestitures, which were previously included in our Industrial Solutions segment, for pre-divestiture periods in 2025; costs associated with CEO transition activities, including severance and executive recruitment costs; and costs related to significant or unusual litigation matters, including legal fees, claim-related judgments and settlements. Amortization of intangibles and acquisition and divestiture-related costs are excluded from non-GAAP measures as the timing and magnitude of business combination transactions are not predictable, can vary significantly from period to period and the purchase price allocated to amortizable intangible assets and the related amortization period are unique to each acquisition. Amortization of intangible assets will recur in future periods until such intangible assets have been fully amortized. While intangible assets contribute to the Company’s revenue generation, the amortization of intangible assets does not directly relate to the sale of the Company’s products or services. Additionally, intangible assets amortization expense typically fluctuates based on the size and timing of the Company’s acquisition activity. Accordingly, the Company believes excluding the amortization of intangible assets enhances the Company’s and investors’ ability to compare the Company’s past financial performance with its current performance and to analyze underlying business performance and trends. Although stock-based compensation is a key incentive offered to certain of our employees, the expense is non-cash in nature, and we continue to evaluate our business performance excluding stock-based compensation; therefore, it is excluded from non-GAAP measures. Stock-based compensation expenses will recur in future periods. Charges related to restructuring and cost optimization plans, impairment charges, including goodwill, divestiture gains or losses, and the costs, including legal fees, related to significant or unusual litigation matters are excluded from non-GAAP measures as the frequency and magnitude of these activities may vary widely from period to period. Additionally, impairment charges, including goodwill, are non-cash. Furthermore, the Company believes the costs, including legal fees, related to significant or unusual litigation matters are not indicative of our core business' operations. The matters discussed above are tax effected, as applicable, in calculating non-GAAP diluted income (loss) per share. Adjusted EBITDA, defined as net (loss) income, plus income tax (provision) benefit, interest and other income (expense), net, stock-based compensation expense, amortization of intangible assets, depreciation expense, and other non-GAAP adjustments, all as described above, is used by management to evaluate performance and helps measure financial performance period-over-period. Furthermore, in this press release, 3D Systems reports certain non-GAAP financial measures further adjusted to remove the operating activity related to (i) Geomagic, which the Company divested on April 1, 2025, for $119.4 million in cash, and (ii) 3DXpert and Oqton, which the Company divested on October 31, 2025, for $3.3 million in cash plus a revenue-based royalty of up to $12.9 million (together with Geomagic, the "Software Divestitures"), for periods non-comparable on a year over year basis. The Company believes excluding non-comparable periods allows it to include the operating activity related to Software Divestitures only to the extent that results are comparable year over year.
